summary: Using the E2g1–A1g separation (Lee 2010 calibration, same laser and substrate), B is a monolayer (19.23 cm-1), A is a bilayer (21.43), D is about 4L (24.27) and C is bulk-like (25.07). The flakes are thickness-ordered B < A < D < C. The Si-normalised MoS2 intensity supports that order, and the A1g width also falls from A to C. D versus 3L or bulk, and C versus roughly 5L or more, are only weakly resolved, because 3L, 4L and bulk differ by about 1 cm-1 and the instrument resolution is 2.7 cm-1. The spectra show no evidence of defects, and no strain or doping can be identified at the roughly ±0.5 cm-1 level. The thickness assignments need AFM, or low-frequency shear and breathing modes, to confirm.

observations.evidence: Raw fits: E2g1/E' 383.91±0.03, A1g/A1' 403.14±0.10, so Delta = 19.23±0.10 cm-1 (Lee 1L: 19.1). apply_relation gives 1L, confidence high. A1g FWHM 4.75. Weakest MoS2 signal relative to Si: E2g area / Si area = 0.24.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b

observations.evidence: Raw: E2g1 383.37±0.02, A1g 404.80±0.07, Delta = 21.43±0.08 cm-1 (Lee 2L: 21.4); relation gives 2L, confidence high. A1g is the broadest line of the set (FWHM 6.16±0.29), consistent with the reported A1g broadening toward 2L. Si-normalised MoS2 area ratio 0.59, between B and D.
observations.source: Lee 2010, Fig. 2b and p.4 (A1g width 3–6 cm-1 from 6L to 2L)

observations.finding: Flake D is about 4L. The separation overlaps 3L and bulk within about 1 cm-1, so a thicker flake cannot be excluded.
observations.evidence: Raw: E2g1 382.37±0.01, A1g 406.64±0.03, Delta = 24.27±0.03 cm-1 (Lee 4L: 24.3, 3L: 23.1, bulk: 25.2). Relation gives 4L, confidence moderate. Statistical error is tiny, but calibration and resolution give a systematic uncertainty of about 0.3–0.5 cm-1. A1g FWHM 4.45; Si-normalised area ratio 1.57.

observations.finding: Flake C is bulk-like (more than about 5L), the thickest of the four.
observations.evidence: Raw: E2g1 382.24±0.04, A1g 407.31±0.06, Delta = 25.07±0.08 cm-1 (bulk 25.2); relation gives bulk, confidence moderate. A1g is narrow (FWHM 2.86±0.21 vs 4.5–6.2 in the thinner flakes). Highest Si-normalised MoS2/Si area ratio (about 2.1, with roughly 15% uncertainty from the weak Si line), and the Si line is strongly attenuated (height 74 vs 940–1650 in the others).
observations.source: Lee 2010, Fig. 2b; Si-normalised intensity: Li S.-L. et al., arXiv:1308.3835

observations.finding: Thickness trend: E2g1 softens and A1g stiffens with N, with Delta of 19.2, 21.4, 24.3 and 25.1 cm-1 for B, A, D and C. E2g1 FWHM is constant at 2.04–2.12 cm-1, probably resolution-limited, and the E2g1 position barely distinguishes the flakes.
observations.evidence: Raw E2g1 positions 383.91 (B), 383.37 (A), 382.37 (D), 382.24 (C). Raw A1g positions 403.14, 404.80, 406.64, 407.31. E2g1 FWHM 2.04–2.12 in all four. Nominal resolution is 2.7 cm-1, so widths and small shifts are close to the instrument limit.

observations.finding: Calibration: every spectrum with a measurable Si line shows the same Si offset, and it cancels in the separations.
observations.evidence: Si line 520.02, 520.00 and 519.99 cm-1 in A, B and D (offset -0.68 to -0.71 from 520.7). C's Si line is weak, 519.94±0.29, giving -0.76 only from the series fit. A rigid offset like this is calibration or convention, not sample physics. Raw positions match Lee's table to within about 0.1 cm-1 for all four flakes, so I quote raw values. Si-corrected positions are 0.7 higher.

observations.finding: No defect, strain or doping signature can be claimed.
observations.evidence: No distinct LA(M) near 227 cm-1 above the noise (local noise about 20–24 counts) in any spectrum, and no 2LA, 286 or 471 bands. Fitted broad features at 222 cm-1 (flake B) and 321/330 cm-1 (flake D) have errors larger than their values (FWHM 33–65 cm-1) and are baseline curvature, not phonons. E2g1 widths are equal and resolution-limited in all four flakes. Any shift in the separations is accounted for by the layer-number trend, not by strain or doping.
observations.source: Mignuzzi et al. 2015, PRB 91, 195411 (LA(M) as defect band); Scheuschner et al. 2015, PRB 91, 235409 (286/471 bands, mainly UV-excited)

observations.finding: Flake C's spectrum has a cosmic-ray spike at 265.1 cm-1 (removed, not a peak) and is noisy (SNR 19). The E1g mode is forbidden in this backscattering geometry, so its absence is expected.
observations.evidence: rl_qc: 1 spike at 265.1 cm-1 in C. Strongest-band SNR is 56, 70, 19 and 111 for A, B, C and D. E1g is forbidden in basal-plane backscattering.
observations.source: Zhang X. et al. 2015, Chem. Soc. Rev. 44, 2757, arXiv:1502.00701, p.3 and p.6

properties.name: phase
properties.value: 2H (all four; consistent with the exfoliated natural molybdenite source; low-frequency modes were not measured, so 3R is not excluded)
properties.source: Ranjuna et al. 2023, Sci. Rep. 13, 16418, Fig. 1d–f (2H vs 3R distinguished only in the low-frequency modes)

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: none detected / low (no LA(M) at 227 cm-1 above the noise; E2g1 widths resolution-limited)

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: Conley et al. 2013, Nano Lett. 13, 3626 (strain would shift and split E2g1)

properties.name: doping_type
properties.source: Chakraborty et al. 2012, PRB 85, 161403 (doping would shift and broaden A1g)

caveats: Separation to layer number is only unambiguous up to about 2L to 3L. 3L, 4L and bulk differ by about 1 cm-1, close to the 2.7 cm-1 resolution and to the roughly 0.3 cm-1 calibration scatter. D = 4L and C = bulk are therefore weaker assignments than A = 2L and B = 1L.
The reference table comes from one study (Lee 2010). Positions in that table were read from a figure to about ±0.3 cm-1 (the reference-mode lookup in the analysis tools states this).

Strain, doping and substrate each shift E2g1 and A1g and so change Delta. A flake with doped or strained A1g could be misassigned by one layer. These spectra cannot separate such effects from thickness without a second observable.

Absolute intensity is not a thickness measure on 285 nm SiO2/Si, because interference modulates it. Only the Si-normalised ratio is monotonic with N. Here it is computed from fitted areas with a very weak Si line in C, so that value is an order-of-magnitude indicator only.

Raw positions agree with Lee's table, but Si-corrected positions are 0.7 cm-1 higher. Which convention Lee's absolute values used is not known, so absolute shifts of about 0.5 cm-1 are not interpretable. Only the separation is robust.

The E2g1 width of 2.0–2.1 cm-1 is below the stated 2.7 cm-1 resolution. It is probably Lorentzian-fit idealisation, or the real resolution is better than quoted, so linewidths are close to resolution-limited and should not be over-read.

Repeated laser exposure in air can shift A1g by about +1.4 cm-1 and E2g1 by about -1 cm-1 (Bera et al. 2017, arXiv:1707.09386), and heating redshifts both modes. Power was not stated, so a small part of the A1g and E2g1 differences could be exposure history rather than thickness.
The layer-number reading is not affected by laser heating at 40x for single scans on supported flakes, but this was not tested here because no power series is available.
questions_for_user: What laser power at the sample and what exposure time per spectrum? Heating or exposure-induced healing shifts A1g and E2g1 by about 1 cm-1, the same size as a layer step.
Is the low-frequency region below 150 cm-1 accessible with a notch or edge filter change? Shear and breathing modes would decide 3L, 4L and bulk, and 2H against 3R, for flakes C and D.
Do you have AFM, optical contrast or Si-intensity maps for the same flakes? Thickness from AFM would anchor the D = 4L versus bulk call.
Were the spectra taken on single spots, and is the 285 nm SiO2 thickness measured? The oxide thickness changes the interference-driven intensity ratios.
Why is flake C noisy and low in intensity (SNR 19)? Was the acquisition shorter, or was the flake out of focus? This affects the weak Si line used for its normalisation.
Polarization configuration? A1g should vanish in crossed geometry and E2g1 stays, which would separate overlapping modes if a shoulder appears.

limits: Layer numbers for D (about 4L) and C (bulk) rest on a 1 cm-1 step between 3L, 4L and bulk. The data cannot exclude D = 3L or bulk, or C being anywhere above about 5L, without low-frequency modes or AFM.
The data start at 150 cm-1, so shear and breathing modes are not observable. Their absence says nothing about stacking, and 2H versus 3R cannot be checked from these spectra.
One calibration source (Lee 2010) gives the reference table. I did not retrieve its Fig. 2b myself, and values were read from the tool's reference entry, not checked against the paper.
Strain, doping and heating cannot be excluded at the ±0.5 cm-1 level, because Delta and absolute positions change together with N.
A power series, polarization series or a second excitation line was not available, so those hypotheses could not be tested.
Optical appearance (flake colours) was not connected to thickness, since no images were provided. Only the Raman results are reported.
